2. Learned counsel for the respondents submitted that the controversy involved in the present case is squarely covered by a Division Bench judgment dated 05.02.2022 rendered in a batch of Writ Petitions led by "Sushila Kankariya v. State of Rajasthan & Ors." (D.B. Civil Writ Petition No.5916/2021) whereby the impugned action of the respondents in issuing the notification dated 14.06.2016 has been upheld.

entities.text: Sushila Kankariya v. State of Rajasthan & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the respondents though was not in a position to refute the aforesaid submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioners however, he contended that the hon'ble Court in the judgment rendered in the case of Sushila Kankariya (supra) has not considered various important issues of law including the definition of 'Appropriate Government' given under Section 3(e)(v) of the Act of 2013.
He submitted that in the absence of any consideration/discussion on the aforesaid issue, [2024:RJ-JD:33895-DB] (4 of 5) [CW-3627/2019] the said judgment cannot be a binding precedent.
Learned counsel thus requested that the matter may be heard afresh on merits.

4. Heard.
5.

Having gone through the judgment passed by the co- ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Sushila Kankariya (supra), this Court finds that an exactly identical issue has been decided in the said judgment.

The judgment passed by the co- ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Sushila Kankariya (supra) will be a binding precedent and the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioners that some issues raised in the present writ petitions were not examined in the earlier judgment, is absolutely without substance.

An argument raised by learned counsel for the petitioner merely in a different way but with the same effect and construction cannot be made a ground to revisit the earlier order passed by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of Gujarat v. R.A. Mehta reported in (2013) 3 SCC 1 in para 61 pleased to held as under:-
"61.

entities.text: State of Gujarat v. R.A. Mehta reported in (2013) 3 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There can be no dispute with respect to the settled legal proposition that a judgment of this Court is binding, particularly when the same is that of a coordinate Bench or of a larger Bench.

It is also correct to state that even if a particular issue has not been agitated earlier or a particular argument was advanced but was not considered the said judgment does not lose its binding effect, provided that the point with reference to which an argument is subsequently advanced has actually been decided.
The decision therefore, would not lose its authority "merely because it was badly argued, inadequately considered or fallaciously reasoned."

The case must be considered taking note of the ratio decidendi of the same i.e. the general reasons or the general grounds upon which the decision of the court is [2024:RJ-JD:33895-DB]
(5 of 5) [CW-3627/2019] based, or on the test or abstract from the specific peculiarities of the particular case which finally gives rise to the decision."
6. In wake of the discussion made hereinabove, these Writ Petitions are hereby dismissed as being devoid of merit.
